quick.summary: Why feedback feels like an attack, and how to focus on facts.
quick.takeaway: Describe what happened to the system, not the person who did it.

beats.line: I told a developer their queries were incredibly messy. Why did they get angry?
Imagine a doctor. A doctor looks at a broken arm.
They say the bone is fractured. They do not say you are clumsy.
But the queries really were slowing down the whole database.
Then talk about the database speed, not the developer.
We call this fundamental attribution error.
Can I just say focus on the problem?
Focus on the problem is exactly right.
Describe what happened to the system, not the person who did it.
I will say the query took ten minutes, instead of calling it messy.

quiz.question: Which of these is the most effective way to give feedback on a failure?
options: The memory usage spiked when the script ran.
You were not careful enough with memory limits.
Your script is incredibly inefficient right now.
You need to pay more attention during deployment.
quiz.explanation: Stating the exact technical outcome separates the problem from the person, preventing defensiveness.

quiz.question: If someone makes a mistake, it is helpful to gently point out their personal flaws.
quiz.explanation: Always focus on the behavior or the system outcome, never on personal traits.
